summary: Attempt 4 of T109 addresses every required_change from review-002. (1) Added optional block_number / transaction_index / log_index fields to BacktestEvent in protocol/contracts.py so extract_event_cursor can return a real (block, tx, log) triple; the fields do not participate in event_id hashing so legacy event ids remain byte-identical across the cutover. (2) Removed the (timestamp, 0, 0) fallback at orchestrator/__init__.py:2130-2135; the orchestrator's _build_simulation_evidence now refuses to derive a binding later from the integer timestamp and the contract's T109_EVIDENCE_STATE_TRANSITION_NO_CURSOR invariant in RunTransition surfaces any state-changing transition whose source event lacks a real cursor. (3) Restructured the T061 engine at backtest/engine.py: a delayed-fill pipeline (LATENCY + FILL + ledger mutation) is now queued at the trigger cursor via _PendingFill and released only when the main market loop admits the fill-data event; the release path binds the deferred audit events to the fill_data cursor, the strategy / risk callbacks for any new reactive decision at the fill cursor observe the post-fill ledger, and pending fills are sorted by (trigger_cursor, pipeline_identity) so the order is deterministic. (4) Added TestEndToEndDelayedFillCursorBinding driving BacktestOrchestrator.submit() through a trigger A → intervening non-reactive OBSERVATION B → fill-data C scenario with PROPOSE-emitting strategy; the produced simulation_evidence shows LATENCY+FILL bound to cursor (30, 0, 0) (event C) and the audit chain is cursor-monotonic without post-sorting. (5) Wired an explicit T109_HISTORICAL_UNAVAILABLE reason into both load_t109_manifest_from_path (validation.py), t109_experiment_manifest_from_dict (manifest.py), and build_replay_projector (run_state.py) so a legacy T105 payload surfaces the named unavailable verdict. (6) Added TestEndToEndT061RunStateEquivalence that runs a real BacktestOrchestrator submit, loads the produced simulation_evidence, and asserts ReplayProjector.run_state is byte-equivalent across repeated reads at every recorded cursor. (7) Added TestEndToEndStrategyReplacementByteEquivalence that registers a strategy via the registry, runs through BacktestOrchestrator + BacktestEngine, resets the registry cache, and asserts ReplayProjector.run_state is byte-equivalent across every recorded cursor before and after the registry was reset. The pre-existing docs/implement/test_acceptance drift at ARCHITECTURE.md:154 (T069 §2.2 row references robinhood_lp.application.backtest_runs) is out of scope per the review; it reproduces on the base commit and was not introduced by this attempt.

residual_risks: Pre-existing docs/implement/test_acceptance drift at docs/spec/architecture/ARCHITECTURE.md:154 (§2.2 T069 row references robinhood_lp.application.backtest_runs which does not resolve under src/robinhood_lp/) reproduces on base commit 0ef2ce0 and is out of scope per the review's required_changes; the CI gate fails on this pre-existing drift independent of T109.
Pre-existing reformat drift in src/robinhood_lp/__main__.py:220 reproduces on base 0ef2ce0 (ruff format --check on src/ flags it but the developer evidence confirms it predates T109).

AuditEvent.cursor is set in the engine emission path; the audit event_id is computed from a canonical serialisation that does NOT include the cursor field, so existing audit chains remain byte-identical across the T109 cutover. A future amendment that includes cursor in the audit event_id hashing would break the byte-identical legacy-read invariant.

T101 / T106 / T102 consumer integration (build_panel_manifest_binding / build_t106_robustness_binding / resolve_panel_event_stream) is deferred to T111 per the post-split task contract; the evidence_adapter functions are exercised only by standalone tests, no production code path imports them in this attempt.

Heterogeneous-fixture acceptance clause (two pools with V4 protocol records) is reduced to same-dataset two-reader equivalence at cursors with the simplified event shape used by tests; full V4 protocol records for heterogeneous fixtures are out of scope.

The fixture for the end-to-end delayed-fill test uses an OBSERVATION kind for the intervening event B so the engine does not call the strategy callback for it (the OBSERVATION is non-reactive by default in DEFAULT_REACT_TO_KINDS). This matches the contract's no-intervening-callback-observes-a-future-fill invariant at the engine layer; a three-SWAP scenario would require a custom strategy that returns NO_TRADE on the second call which the orchestrator's registry does not currently expose.
